chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us from al-Zuhri.

He said: I was with 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and a man from his companions came to him. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: What news do you bring, O man? The man said: My news — O son of the Messenger of Allah — is that I have incurred a debt of four hundred gold coins, and I have no means to pay it off. I have weighty dependants and I have nothing to provide for them. He said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) wept intensely. I said to him: What makes you weep, O son of the Messenger of Allah? He said: Is weeping not reserved for afflictions and great hardships? They said: Indeed it is, O son of the Messenger of Allah. He said: What hardship and affliction is greater for the sanctity of a believer than to see his believing brother in a difficulty he cannot alleviate, and to witness him in poverty he cannot lift?

He said: They then dispersed from that gathering. One of the opponents who used to slander 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: How astonishing are these people — on one occasion they claim that the heavens, the earth, and everything obey them and that Allah does not reject any of their requests, then on another occasion they admit to being unable to rectify the situations of the closest of their brothers! News of that reached the man of the story. He went to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, I was told that so-and-so said such-and-such, and that was harder on me than my difficult situation. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: Allah has permitted your relief. O so-and-so, bring my pre-dawn meal (suhur) and my breakfast (futur). She brought two morsels of bread. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to the man: Take them, for we have nothing else. Allah will relieve you through them and grant you vast goodness through them.

The man took them and went to the market not knowing what to do with them, pondering the weight of his debt and the condition of his dependants. Satan whispered to him: What good are these two in the face of your need? He passed by a fishmonger who had a fish that had gone bad and couldn't be sold. He said to him: Your fish is no good to you, and one of these morsels is no good to me — would you give me your bad fish in exchange for my bad morsel? The man said: Yes. So he gave him the fish and took the morsel. Then he passed by a man with a small amount of salt that no one wanted. He said to him: Would you give me this unwanted salt in exchange for this unwanted morsel? He said: Yes. So the man had the fish and the salt. He said: I will preserve this with that. When he split open the belly of the fish, he found in it two magnificent pearls. He praised Allah for them. While he was in that joy, there was a knock at his door. He went out to see who was at the door; the fishmonger and the salt-seller had come. Each of them said to him: O servant of Allah, we and our families tried to eat this morsel but our teeth could not manage it. We think you must have reached an extreme of misfortune and grown accustomed to wretchedness. We return this bread to you and release to you what you took from us. He took the two morsels from them.

After they had left and he had settled, there was a knock at his door. It was the messenger of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He entered and said: He says to you: Allah has brought you relief, so return our food to us, for none but us can eat it. The man sold the two pearls for great wealth, paid off his debt, and after that his condition improved. One of the opponents said: How extreme is this disparity! While 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was unable to relieve his poverty, he enriched him with this great wealth. How can this be? How can he who is able to bestow such great wealth be incapable of relieving poverty?

'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: This is what the Quraysh said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): How can he travel from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis, witness the relics of the prophets within it, and return to Mecca in a single night — he who could not travel from Mecca to Medina except in twelve days? That was said when he had emigrated from it.

Then 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: By Allah, they are ignorant of the command of Allah and the command of His friends with Him. Verily, the exalted ranks cannot be attained except through submission to Allah — Exalted be His praise — abandoning proposals contrary to Him, and being content with how He manages their affairs. Indeed, the friends of Allah endure hardships and adversities with a patience that none other than them can match. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic — rewards them for that by guaranteeing the success of all their requests. Yet with all that, they only desire from Him what He desires for them.

key_terms.أولياء الله: The friends/guardians of Allah — referring to the Imams and those close to God who have attained special status
key_terms.الاقتراح: Proposing or demanding — here used to mean imposing one's own wishes on God rather than accepting His plan
key_terms.التسليم: Submission — complete surrender to God's will as the prerequisite for spiritual elevation
key_terms.الفرج: Relief, divine opening after hardship — a key concept in Shia theology emphasizing that God's deliverance comes from unexpected sources
key_terms.المخالفين: Opponents — here referring to those who disputed the special status and authority of Imam Zayn al-Abidin
key_terms.المراتب الرفيعة: The exalted ranks — the highest spiritual stations attained by the Awliya'

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Zayn al-Abidin and the man with four hundred gold dinars of debt?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) responded to a companion burdened with four hundred gold dinars of debt. The Imam wept for his brother's plight, gave him his only food — two morsels of bread — which miraculously multiplied into two precious pearls found inside a fish, allowing the man to pay off his debt. When opponents mocked the apparent contradiction between the Imam's claimed authority and his apparent inability to immediately solve poverty, the Imam responded by comparing it to the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra'), explaining that the exalted status of the Awliya' of Allah is attained through complete submission, patience, and contentment with Divine decree — and that they only ever desire what Allah wills for them.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Qasim al-Astarabadi narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Abu Yahya Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Sufyan b. `Uyayna narrated to us from al-Zuhri.

He said: I was with `Ali b. al-Husayn (as), and a man from his companions had come to him. So, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said to him: What news do you bring, man? So, the man said: My news – O son of the Messenger of Allah – is that I have incurred a debt of four hundred gold coins, and I do not have the means to pay it off. I have weighty dependants, and I do not have that which I owe them. He said: So, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) wept intensely. So, I said to him: What makes you weep, O son of the Messenger of Allah? So, he said: Doesn’t one weep after afflictions and great hardships? They said: Yes, O son of the Messenger of Allah. He said: So, what hardship or affliction is greater for the sanctity of the believer than to see his believing brother in a difficulty that he cannot stop and witness a poverty that he cannot uplift himself from?!

He said: So, they left their gathering upon that. He said: So, one of the opponents (mukhalifin) who would insult `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said: It is astonishing that these, who, in one instance, claim that the heavens and the Earth and all things obey them, and that Allah does not reject their requests, then in another instance, admit to being unable to rectify the situations of the choicest of their brothers. [News of] that came to the man related to the story. So, he went to `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! I was informed that so-and-so said such-and-such, and that was harder on me than my difficult situation. So, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said [to his maidservant]: May Allah relieve you, so-and-so, hold up my pre-fasting meal (suhur) and my breakfast (futur). So, she held up two morsels. Then, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said to the man: Take this, for we have nothing else but this. Allah will relieve you through this, and He will give you expansive goodness through this.

So, the man took them (the two morsels) and went to the market not knowing what to do with them. He was thinking about the weight of his debt and the condition of his dependants. Satan whispered to him: What is the status of these two [meals] in comparison to your need? So, he passed by a fish seller who had a fish with an odour. So, he said to him: This fish of yours is no good for you, and this morsel is no good for me, so would you trade your no-good fish for my no-good morsel? So, he said: Yes. So, he took the fish and had one morsel remaining. Then, he passed by a man who had a small amount of salt. So, he said to him: Would you trade this small amount of salt for this small morsel? He said: Yes. So, the man had fish and salt, and said: I will rectify this [fish] with this [salt]. When he cut the stomach of the fish, he found two luxurious pearls in it. He praised Allah for them. He went back to his house, and there was a knock on his door. He went out to see who was at the door. He found that the fish seller and the salt seller had come, each of whom said: O servant of Allah! We and our dependants tried eating this morsel, but our teeth could not handle it. We know that you are in a bad condition and that you are forbearing misery. So, we return this bread to you, and we want you to keep what you have taken from us. So, he took the two morsels from them.

After they left, there was a knock on his door. He found the messenger of `Ali b. al-Husayn (as), who entered and said: He says to you: “Surely, Allah has given you relief, so return our food to us, for none but us can eat it.” So, the man sold the pearls for great wealth and paid off his debt. After that, his condition improved. So, one of the opponents said: How severe is this disparity! We thought that `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) was unable to rectify his poverty, but he enriched him with great wealth. How can this be? How can he be unable to rectify poverty when he can enrich this person with great wealth?

So, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said: This is what Quraysh said to the Prophet (s): How can he go from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis and witness what is in it of the relics of the prophets; and return to it in one night? It took him twelve days to go from Mecca to Medina. [He said:] That was [said] after he had emigrated from it.

Then, `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) said: They are ignorant of the order of Allah and the order of His friends with Him. Surely, the exalted ranks cannot be reached except by submitting to Allah, abandoning proposals [that are contrary] to Him, and being content with what He plans for you. Surely, the friends of Allah are patient with adversity and misfortunes in a way that others are not, so because of that, Allah grants them success in all their requests. However, with that, they only want from Him what He wants for them.
